objective: Verify that the Request filter dropdown displays only active suppression filters and that edit and duplicate request flows correctly handle inactive filters as described.

features_to_test.detail: Dropdown lists only active suppression filters; inactive filters are excluded
When editing, an inactive selected filter remains visible; saving without change shows error popup; user can select active filter and save successfully
Duplicating a request with an inactive filter allows duplication; on save an error popup is shown; user can select active filter and save successfully

design_techniques.why: Separate active vs inactive filter states
Cover combinations of edit/duplicate actions with active/inactive filters
Validate transitions from view to edit/duplicate to save with error handling

execution_phases.focus: Functional validation of edit and duplicate flows
Regression run covering existing request features

entry_criteria: Code build deployed to a test environment
Test data for active and inactive suppression filters prepared
exit_criteria: All critical defects resolved or deferred with agreement

risks.risk: Missing or inaccurate filter status data in test environment
risks.mitigation: Coordinate with data team to seed known active/inactive filters before testing

risks.risk: Error popup UI not implemented as expected
risks.mitigation: Confirm design mockup or specification with product owner early

assumptions: The application distinguishes active vs inactive suppression filters in the backend
Error pop‑up mechanism exists and can display custom messages

gaps.question_for_author: Please provide explicit acceptance criteria for each behavior (filter dropdown, edit request, duplicate request) including expected messages and success conditions.
